_comment: TARGET-tier scope definition for the `src` target of libgit2 1.9.0.
Port scope is the whole shipped source tree - the library (src/libgit2,
src/util), the CLI (src/cli), and the public headers under include/.
_comment_files: `files.port` names everything the port scope contains - there is no
implicit directory walk, so `src/` is listed alongside `include/` rather
than being inherited from the target id.
Both entries are directories because every file beneath them is
port-scope, which orchestrator.md prefers over enumerating files.
Why include/ qualifies (the implementor test from orchestrator.md,
'Setting up scope targets'): headers outside the target tree belong in
port scope only when the code that IMPLEMENTS what they declare is
itself port-scope. include/git2/*.h declares libgit2's public API and
its public value structs (git_oid, git_strarray, git_diff_options,
git_checkout_options, ...), all implemented under src/libgit2 and
src/util. include/git2/sys/*.h declares the plugin/backend vtable
structs, and their implementors are port-scope too - verified rather
than assumed: git_odb_backend -> src/libgit2/odb_loose.c, odb_pack.c,
odb_mempack.c; git_refdb_backend -> refdb_fs.c, refdb_reftable.c;
git_config_backend -> config_file.c, config_mem.c; git_transport ->
transports/*.c; git_filter -> crlf.c, ident.c, filter.c. No header under
include/ is a pure consumer or referencer, so the whole directory goes
in and no file-level split is needed.
Deliberately NOT listed, and therefore wrap-scope (FFI) rather than
port-scope: deps/xdiff, deps/reftable and deps/ntlmclient. Those three
compile into libgit2.so (see build.json) but cannot be de-vendored, and
they are vendored third-party C rather than libgit2's own code, so they
belong behind the C/FFI bridge. The three deps that COULD be de-vendored
- zlib, pcre2, llhttp - are system libraries in this configuration and
are not in the CodeQL database at all.
Also not listed: tests/ and deps/clar. The traced build sets
BUILD_TESTS=OFF, so they contribute no entities to the database.
`files.wrap` is empty: every FFI dependency this port reaches is derived
as the import closure of `files.port`. It would name public headers to
wrap outright, which is what a wrap-only target consists of.
_comment_out_of_scope: `paths` is empty on purpose. The candidates one might reflexively list
here are already excluded by construction: tests/ and deps/clar are not
in the traced build; deps/{xdiff,reftable,ntlmclient} are outside
port_files and so land in wrap scope, which is where they belong;
are globbed into the build by cmake but emptied out by #ifdefs, and
scope.json is anchored on the T1 tables, so a body elided by a disabled
feature contributes no entities and drops out on its own.
`features` is documentation only - no composer reads it. It lists the
feature macros that are OFF in this build, mirroring build.json's
features.all entries whose `enabled` is false. The authoritative record
